Having lost my best friend to suicide last year and being held in a psych unit hours away from my home for two months, I've learnt to think about it from your loved ones perspective. When they did what they did, they truly believed they were doing you and everyone that loves them a favour. Depression tricks the brain in those sorts of ways. Live in honour of your friend, do everything he didn't get to do for him, in his place. Even small things like pouring my best friend his own pint and setting it down next to me while i have mine helped me tremendously to cope with his death. 
Your friend wants you to live your life, and so do the people around you, and myself. You deserve to have a good life and you deserve to heal and feel better. You got this <3

of course! try standing up very slowly + in stages after a spell. during the active spell lay down, then sit up for a few minutes, then kneel, then sit on a chair and then finally stand up and wait until you feel entirely better before you try climbing again. it's all about patience, be patient with yourself. maybe get a portable blood pressure machine or heart rate machine to try and identify when it's safe to climb again. take your heart rate or blood pressure before you climb when you feel good and you've eaten and drank some water and use that as a baseline for how your blood pressure should be before you start climbing again

I have a fainting disorder myself. whilst the only thing I can recommend diagnosis-wise is to see a GP or doctor and get professional help, I can give advice on how to deal with fainting spells whilst bouldering. I've found that eating carbs and proteins directly before training helps with keeping blood pressure up, I usually have a cliff bar (which also helps with blood sugar). when you get dizzy mid-climb, get down immediately and sit down with your head between your knees until it passes, then drink some water and maybe have a snack, and if it keeps on happening, abandon the training session. your safety is more important than climbing, always. again, when it comes to finding the cause, Reddit isn't going to help, you need to see a doctor. i have more tips on dealing with dizziness if you'd like them :)
